assertions.text: Output contains at least 2 separate markdown tables (not everything crammed into one table)
assertions.evidence: The response contains only one markdown table under '### Plans' with columns: Plan | Price | Billing cycle. Additional content is in narrative text or code blocks, not separate markdown tables.

assertions.text: The tables cover distinct concerns — e.g. pricing/plans is separate from cancellation/refund rules
assertions.evidence: Only one markdown table exists (the Plans table). Cancellation and refund rules are covered in narrative text sections, not in separate tables.

assertions.text: At least one output column in each table ends with '?'
assertions.evidence: The Plans table columns are: 'Plan', 'Price', 'Billing cycle'. None end with '?'. No output columns in the single existing table use the '?' suffix.

assertions.text: The 24-hour no-refund exception is included as a distinct scenario row
assertions.evidence: The 24-hour exception is described as 'Exception — cancel within 24 hours of a renewal charge: No refund issued.' under narrative text, not as a distinct row in a scenario/example table.

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language — no implementation terms like 'boolean', 'int', 'isProrated', camelCase identifiers
assertions.evidence: The Plans table uses columns: 'Plan', 'Price', 'Billing cycle' — all business-friendly language without technical jargon or camelCase.

assertions.text: Includes a row or scenario for cancelling during the free trial — no charge was made, so no refund applies. This case should be explicit, not omitted.
assertions.evidence: Trial cancellation is covered in narrative text: 'Cancellation during trial: No refund (no charge was made).' under the Cancellation & Refunds section, not as a distinct table row.

assertions.text: The prorated refund calculation is shown or explained — e.g. days remaining × daily rate, or an equivalent formula. Not just 'prorated refund' without showing how.
assertions.evidence: Formula shown: 'refund = (price / cycle_days) × days_remaining' with example: 'Subscriber on annual (£95.88), cancels with 200 days remaining... daily_rate = 95.88 / 365 = £0.2627, refund = ceil(200) × 0.2627 = £52.54'

assertions.text: The 24-hour no-refund window is tested near the boundary (e.g. values at or close to 23h, 24h, 25h) — not just 'within 24h' vs 'well after renewal'.
assertions.evidence: Only one example given: 'Subscriber cancels 10 hours after a renewal charge → **no refund**'. No systematic boundary testing at 23h, 24h, or 25h thresholds.

assertions.text: Refund eligibility (yes/no, based on 24h rule and trial status) and refund amount (prorated calculation) are in separate tables — not mixed into one table.
assertions.evidence: No tables exist showing refund eligibility scenarios or refund amounts as separate tables. Eligibility rules and amount calculations are described in narrative text and formulas, not in structured example tables.

assertions.text: The '?' suffix is only used on output/expected columns (e.g. 'Refund Eligible?', 'Refund Amount?') — not on input columns like plan type, loyalty status, or yes/no flags.
assertions.evidence: No '?' suffixes appear anywhere in the response. The rule requiring '?' only on output columns (not input columns) is satisfied by the absence of any violations.
